title: Prevent duplicate billing with watermark fence commit protocol
creator: Luca Fernandez
description: Background: Customers occasionally see duplicate token consumption when clients retry requests (timeout/retry or at-least-once delivery from edge). Existing defenses partially rely on client-supplied nonces and best-effort de-duplication in the ingestion layer, but race windows and cross-region failover still permit double-billing. Goal: Design and implement a server-side commit protocol that provides idempotent billing semantics for inference requests without requiring synchronous cross-region consensus on every request. Approach: introduce a per-customer monotonic request watermark + short-lived commit leases plus a local append-only billing fence ledger. Ingest proxies will accept requests with optional client-provided request_id; server will assign a sequence token when request is first accepted into the local ledger. Billing is only committed when a commit operation (automatic post-response or explicit ack) advances the customer watermark past the sequence token. Retries that replay the same payload will be detected by watermark/ledger and returned as previous-result or treated as idempotent. This protocol aims to achieve exactly-once billing semantics across transient retries while keeping tail latency low and preserving throughput by avoiding global synchronous locks.
acceptance_criteria: No customer sees duplicate billed tokens for a single logical request under common retry scenarios (client retry, LB reconnect, region failover) in 99.99% of test runs
Latency P95 increase for normal requests < 5ms after enabling ledger write path
Backfill reconciliation job can reconcile outstanding ledger entries and either commit or refund within configured SLA (24h default)
SDKs gracefully handle preflight-ack vs postflight-commit semantics and error codes are documented
Automated chaos tests demonstrate correctness under packet loss and delayed acks
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flagged runtime build that writes to local ledger but does not change billing commit: dry-run with logging
Phase 1: Enable commit-on-success for 10% of traffic on low-risk tenants; monitor for anomalies
Phase 2: Ramp to 100% for single-region tenants; enable cross-region reconciliation
Phase 3: Full enable with reconciliation job scheduled; sunset legacy best-effort dedupe after 2 weeks of stable metrics
implementation_notes: Store ledger as append-only segments keyed by customer_id and shard_id; segments are tombstoned after watermark advances
Sequence assignment is local to ingest shard; watermark advances are durable and propagated via async replication
For cross-region failover, a reconciliation sweep will query remote ledgers and apply idempotent commit/refund decisions based on last-known watermark
Provide SDK helper that embeds client_request_id and a small payload fingerprint to improve matching for clients that cannot guarantee monotonic IDs
Edge proxies should attach ingest_shard and assigned_sequence_token in response headers to aid client-side dedupe logic
tests: Unit: ledger append/read/compact correctness under concurrent writes
Integration: deterministic replay tests where client retries after network partition are asserted to not double-bill
Chaos: drop-ack and delayed-commit scenarios across two regions with reconciliation enabled
Load: 2x production throughput to verify ledger can sustain write QPS without impacting latency SLO
E2E: SDK + runtime test that simulates mobile clients with flaky networks and verifies billing idempotency
open_questions: What is the acceptable refund latency for customers in the event of ledger reconciliation declaring duplicates? Current proposal: 24h default, configurable per-tenant
Should committed token accounting be visible in real-time in console ledgers or reflect after reconciliation window?
How do we charge for requests that are served from cache but still consume billing units? (cache-hit attribution needs clarity)
Edge-case: how to handle divergent watermarks if a shard is cut-over mid-request? Need clear handoff protocol
Operational: what runbook actions are required if reconciliation backlog grows past 72h?
